content:
Following the May adjustment to its computing resource usage policy, Google is set to restrict which Gemini models free users and AI Plus subscribers can access.

According to support documents updated this week, Gemini App users without a Google AI subscription will only be able to use the (3.5) Flash-Lite model. From October 9, users who have not paid for a Gemini subscription will no longer be able to use (3.6) Flash or (3.1) Pro.

At the same time, AI Plus subscribers will only be able to use Flash-Lite and Flash, with Pro no longer offered. These users paying US$4.99 per month will "receive emails explaining when the changes will take effect."

Gemini Model Google AI Plan Flash-Lite Flash Pro Without a plan ✓ X X AI Plus ✓ ✓ X AI Pro ✓ ✓ ✓ AI Ultra ✓ ✓ ✓

AI Pro and AI Ultra users, by contrast, will not see any reductions in their usage entitlements. On the contrary, customers paying US$19.99 per month will gain access to the Deep Think option, providing "maximum parallel reasoning" capabilities—a feature currently limited to plans costing US$99.99 and US$199.99 per month.

The most upvoted comment was posted by Glitter Guru

Argon had better replace Pro, otherwise I expect 4 Pro to launch alongside Argon when it goes public. If not, and 3.1 Pro remains the top-tier model for most users, I'll be cancelling my Pro plan.

Using AI Ultra's Gemini 3.1 Pro with Deep Think

In October, the Gemini App also appears to be adding three reasoning intensity options—"Low," "Medium," and "High"—"applicable to every available model."

Currently, users can only enable "Extended Thinking: Solve complex problems." These three new reasoning intensity/thinking levels will correspond to the options offered in Google AI Studio and Antigravity.

How Gemini 4 Argon will be positioned remains unclear. Google announced earlier this week that it will first be made available to AI Ultra subscribers. The company has not indicated whether Argon will be classified as a Pro model or belong to a new tier above Pro.
